hypotheses.title: CFG creation is O(N^2) in the number of match clauses (addEdge duplicate check scans the growing children/parents lists)
hypotheses.issue: functionControlFlowAnalyzer.addEdge deduplicates every edge with slices.Contains over bbs[from].children and bbs[to].parents. analyzeMatch adds one edge from the single match block to each newly created clause block (the match block's children list grows to N) and one edge from each non-terminal clause end to the single shared `finally` merge block (its parents list grows to N). Each insertion linearly scans the growing list, so an N-clause match costs O(N^2) in CFG Creation. The edges added in analyzeMatch can never be duplicates: each clause block is fresh, each clause body ends in a block created while analysing that clause (if/while/foreach/unreachable all create new blocks, break/continue terminate), `finally` is never a loop target, and the non-exhaustive curBB->finally edge is added once. Profile on a 64k-clause match: CFG Creation 1482 ms, ~1.33 s flat in addEdge -> slices.Contains -> slices.Index. Scaling: 89 ms @16k, 368 ms @32k, 1482 ms @64k clauses.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a function with one wide match statement (N const-pattern clauses).
Usage: gen_match.py [N] [out.bal]"""
import sys
N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 40000
out = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "/tmp/perfhunt/H1/wide_match.bal"
with open(out, "w") as f:
    f.write("import ballerina/io;\n\npublic function main() {\n    int x = 3;\n    match x {\n")
    for i in range(N):
        f.write(f"        {i} => {{ io:println({i}); }}\n")
    f.write("        _ => { io:println(-1); }\n    }\n}\n")

python3 gen_match.py 40000 wide_match.bal; go build -tags debug -o /tmp/perfhunt/bal-debug ./cli/cmd; python3 measure.py wide_match.bal  # measure.py: runs `bal-debug run --trace=trace.json <file>` and sums trace event durations per stage. measure.py source:
import sys,json,subprocess,collections,time
f=sys.argv[1]; t="/tmp/perfhunt/H1/trace.json"
t0=time.time(); r=subprocess.run(["/tmp/perfhunt/bal-debug","run","--trace="+t,f],capture_output=True,text=True); wall=time.time()-t0
ev=json.load(open(t)); ev=ev['traceEvents'] if isinstance(ev,dict) else ev
agg=collections.Counter()
for e in ev:
    if 'dur' in e and 'ballerina/' not in e['name']:
        agg[e['name'].rsplit(' ',1)[0]]+=e['dur']
print(f"{f}: rc={r.returncode} wall={wall:.2f}s")
for k,v in agg.most_common(10): print(f"  {k:28s} {v/1000:8.1f} ms")

hypotheses.fix_approach: Added an unchecked addNewEdge(from,to) that appends to children/parents without the slices.Contains scans, documented as requiring the caller to guarantee the edge is new, and used it for the three edge kinds in analyzeMatch (match block -> fresh clause block, clause end -> finally, non-exhaustive match block -> finally). addEdge keeps its dedup for all other callers (if/while/foreach/break/continue). --dump-cfg output was byte-identical to main for all 82 corpus files containing match and for a 20k-clause file; make test passes. Pitfall: the invariant that no two clauses end in the same block relies on every control-flow construct creating fresh continuation blocks; an alternative that avoids relying on it is a per-block edge set (or dedup only when the list is long). The same quadratic pattern could exist for other many-predecessor merge points if one ever gets wide.
